items.title: Elon Musk says: 'I'm not MAGA'
items.snippet: Elon Musk, who spent $277 million to get Donald Trump reelected president in 2024 and who, during that campaign, declared himself “dark MAGA” and who, after the election, was subsequently photographed sporting a cartoonishly large MAGA hat while visiting the Oval Office, has some news for Americans: None of that necessarily makes him MAGA. “I’m not MAGA,” Musk declared Wednesday during a conversation with Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times DealBook Summit. Musk joined the conversation via video call, as he is currently in China, joining President Trump for the APEC summit. “Well, at least I’m not like … I’m not sure what MAGA means,” he backtracked. “If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.” The comments were made amidst a broader question about how Musk felt in the wake of this year’s midterms, during which a “blue wave” led to Democratic victories throughout the country. Starting in April 2027, Google is going to require Android developers to make sure their apps have a baseline level of support for foldables. If they don't, developers risk not being able to publish or update their apps or have reduced visibility for their apps on Google Play. Google says Android apps must meet its "Tier 3 - Adaptive ready" standard. "Apps must fill the available display area without letterboxing or compatibility modes," Google says . However, one new project that has surfaced is using elements that Apple itself developed to create something new. items.title: macOS 27.3’s new Full Disk Access prompt protects your data from apps that want it
items.snippet: Macworld In October, Apple announced that it was going to change how it implements Full Disk Access control in macOS. Users were going to have to perform “very explicit user action” to grant FDA to an app, which is a change from before, when apps could prompt users to flip switches on in System Settings to allow FDA. The change is coming to macOS 27.3, and it was recently unveiled in the macOS 27.3 beta 2 that was released on Monday. Apple released a note to developers notifying them about the change, stating that the changes “empower [users] to make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.” The new FDA UI was posted online by madeby_ldt, and it’s much more detailed and explicit.

items.title: Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour
items.snippet: Nvidia’s GeForce 621.14 and 621.24 drivers reportedly rewrite a log file nonstop, writing gigabytes to SSDs every hour.

items.title: Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal
items.snippet: Interim CEO Collete Kress reportedly offered staffers higher wages and more equity on an advanced schedule at the company's first all-hands after Jensen Huang resigned.

items.title: GTA VI runs at 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but just 720p with upscaling on Series S
items.snippet: GTA VI will target 30FPS across PlayStation and Xbox consoles, with Rockstar using its own temporal anti-aliasing solution on the PS5 and Xbox Series X, Sony's PSSR 2 on the PS5 Pro, and AMD's FSR 4 on the Xbox Series S.

items.title: Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume it predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development
items.snippet: AMD has criticized Nvidia, and to a lesser extent Arm, for claims about creating a CPU designed for agentic AI. Nvidia is pushing back on that characterization, instead saying Vera was designed with “base principles, product intuition, and oftentimes simple allegorical laws of computer science” in a recent interview with Tom’s Hardware.

items.title: The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure
items.snippet: Jensen’s affairs dominated headlines, but the seeds of his downfall were planted in both the bedroom and the boardroom and stretched from Beijing to Washington, with Nvidia sitting right in the middle.

items.title: Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year-over-year in Q3 2026
items.snippet: A TrendForce report reveals that gamers are buying OLED monitors in a big way, and ASUS leads the pack.

items.title: Nvidia board faction angling for Jensen Huang return as CEO, report claims
items.snippet: Despite Nvidia's board saying it has no intention of bringing former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, some directors are reportedly still pushing for that to happen.

items.title: Nvidia's revenue hits $115.8 billion as Vera Rubin generates $20 billion in another record-setting quarter
items.snippet: Nvidia's quarterly revenue surged to $115.8 billion as Vera Rubin achieved a record $20 billion debut, while total commitments to suppliers and customers climbed to $540 billion and rising costs prompted a revised pricing strategy for FY2028.

items.title: Retro Kickstarter speaker can play soundtracks directly from original Game Boy cartridges
items.snippet: Retro Song Bird can play music directly from original cartridges, export individual audio channels to a PC, back up game saves, flash writable cartridges, and sync two units for chiptune DJ performances.

items.title: SSDs, laptops, and phones may get cheaper as consumer NAND spot pricing drops 20%
items.snippet: According to a new report, slowing demand for consumer electronics and diverging production requirements for consumer and enterprise NAND have resulted in declining spot prices for consumer-grade flash memory. Those trends may result in unexpected but welcome relief for consumers.

items.title: Walmart has slashed $700 off this MSI gaming laptop

items.title: $3.26 million in SpaceX AI data center revenue will be pumped back into the City of Memphis
items.snippet: The City of Memphis is making its first major investment, almost $3.3 million, through the Community Benefit Ordinance. The fund was set up to use a portion of the tax generated by SpaceX AI's Colossus 1 facility for the benefit of residents, with the first $2 million allocated for a new home repair assistance program.

items.title: Nvidia employee warns of 'irreplaceable' talent exodus if Jensen Huang not reinstated

items.title: Nvidia claims its Vera CPU can gain up to 39% performance boost via software optimization at SC26 — architectural fine-tuning is needed to fully unleash custom Olympus cores
items.snippet: Nvidia's Vera CPU, powered by its custom Olympus Arm cores, already offers strong performance with unoptimized code, but at SC26, the company demonstrated that further software optimizations can improve performance by nearly 39% with certain workloads.

items.title: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return as Nvidia CEO
items.snippet: In his first statement since his resignation, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed openness to returning to his former role.

items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before a House Foreign Affairs panel amid concerns over his affair with a suspected Chinese spy
items.snippet: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees on December 1, with Nvidia's lawyer following him on December 2. The appearances follow Huang's admission of an affair with a woman who worked for an Nvidia customer who is also believed to be a Chinese spy.

items.title: Taipei 101 lit up in support of Jensen Huang
items.snippet: The Taipei 101 skyscraper was lit up with messages of support for Jensen Huang overnight, the former Nvidia CEO who left the company after admitting to an affair with a former customer who has been accused of being a Chinese Spy. Another affair, this time with an employee, has since been reported.

items.title: AMD attacks Nvidia's FP64 emulation at SC26, touts native double-precision on Instinct MI430X
items.snippet: AMD is touting the benefits of the native FP64 support provided by its MI430X accelerator at Supercomputing 2026. The company says that Ozaki FP64 emulation only covers the needs of a small portion of HPC workloads, making the MI430X a unique foundation for next-gen supercomputing installations.

items.title: Nvidia warns customers of new US rule that could expose them to lawsuits for serving Chinese clients
items.snippet: This warning comes amid Jensen Huang's scandal, a new rule from the U.S. Department of Commerce, and a pending bill in the Senate.

items.title: US government confirms criminal investigation into Singapore company at the heart of Jensen Huang scandal
items.snippet: The Justice and Commerce Departments have announced an investigation into Megaspeed over concerns that it may have been involved in the illegal export of Nvidia's AI hardware. The company was previously run by the woman officials have accused of being a Chinese spy while having an affair with Jensen Huang while he was Nvidia CEO.

items.title: Lose your BitLocker key and Windows 11 can lock you out of your files, so it’ll now warn you when you ditch your Microsoft account for a local one
items.snippet: Windows 11 Build 26340.10013 prompts you to back up your BitLocker recovery key when you switch from a Microsoft account to a local one. Switching won't lock you out, but a later BIOS update or TPM change can, and Microsoft can't recreate a lost key, so save a copy on a USB drive, a file or a printout. items.title: App developers turn to QVAC for AI tooling without the cloud
items.snippet: In most instances today, adding AI to an app means sending user data to a third-party API, paying per request, and hoping the connection holds. Tether’s QVAC is built on the opposite premise. It runs AI models directly on the user’s device. Data never leaves the hardware, there are no per-request costs, no rate limits, and no need for an internet connection once a model is downloaded. QVAC SDK: the next milestone in cloud-free AI While open-source tools and standards like llama.cpp, GGML, and ONNX have made local AI much more accessible in recent years, creating new possibilities for consumer devices, the edge AI ecosystem remains fragmented. items.title: Arista expands its routing options to support secure AI inferencing
items.snippet: Arista is unveiling a portfolio of networking devices designed to secure and improve the performance and resiliency of connections serving AI compute and storage infrastructure. Four new Etherlink R4 high-performance routing switches are aimed at large-scale distributed data center, AI back-end, and service provider environments where high route scale, deep packet buffering, and 400G connectivity are required. In addition, the new R4s integrate line-rate encryption into every port via TunnelSec, including MACsec, IPsec, VXLANsec, and hardware-based Segment Routing over IPv6, according to a blog post co-authored by Brendan Gibbs, Arista vice president, product line management, and Tyson Lamor

items.title: You’ve decided to repatriate cloud workloads. Now what?
items.snippet: For 15 years, enterprise IT moved in one direction: out of the data center and into the public cloud. Hardware teams were trimmed, leases weren’t renewed, and “cloud first” became “cloud only.” That era is ending, not because the cloud failed, but because many organizations never made a placement decision. They made a migration decision and assumed it would fit everything. AI, global macro issues, data ownership, and other trends are prompting IT leadership to rethink their cloud strategy. items.title: Cloud overspend is an accountability problem not a tooling gap
items.snippet: After years of using the clouds, many organizations are coming to realize they didn’t have a proper plan in place from the get-go. Cloud adoption has often been driven by urgency, not design, according to Nabeel Sherif , principal advisory director at Infotech. It accelerated over the past 15 years, especially during the pandemic. Most organizations moved workloads and adopted SaaS, but the operating models behind that work did not change at the same pace. Infrastructure and operations teams, network teams included, now run on-premises and cloud side by side, often without a unifying model.
